title: Synchronized Rewind of Endpoint Heads
statement: Let $L>0$, let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $L+1$ work tapes and Boolean symbols, and let $q_r,q_a$ be states. Suppose that in state $q_r$, on every input and work-tape reading, the machine moves both endpoint heads one cell left and enters $q_r$ if tape zero is nonblank, and moves both one cell right and enters $q_a$ if tape zero is blank; it makes no writes or output. For every Boolean word $w$ and every $j\le |w|$, starting with both endpoint heads at $j-1$, tape zero storing $w$, the last tape blank, and state $q_r$, after exactly $j+1$ steps the configuration has state $q_a$, both endpoint heads at zero, tape zero still storing $w$, and the last tape blank; all other configuration fields agree with the prescribed initial and final two-ended configurations.
hypotheses_covered: A machine on $L+1$ work tapes over Boolean symbols
The stated transition rule holds for every input symbol and work-tape reading
